W1 (mechanism), after E017.

Setup
- Tip E017 = E016 recipe (Muon on conv filters, Lookahead/EMA, 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30%, batch 2000, 238 steps = 9.5 true epochs, widths 128/384/512, SGD wd 0.006, max-autotune + CUDA graphs) with sync/graph-break cleanup.
- Score: 6.548 s, 0.7537. Margin is 0.07 pp.

Big update: noise
- E017 changed no math, yet the mean fell 0.70 pp (0.7607 → 0.7537).
- So any change to kernels or the RNG path reshuffles the 3-seed mean by up to ±0.35 pp. Seed std is about 0.3 pp.
- E016's 0.7607 was a lucky draw. I put the recipe's true mean at about 0.756-0.757 and the expected held-out offset from 0.7607 at about 0.4 pp.
- Consequence: an idea that costs more than about 0.2 pp of true accuracy is more likely than not to measure below 0.753. Measured 'keeps' are partly selection on noise.

Code facts
- Steps: steps_per_epoch = 25 and ceil(9.5 × 25) = 238, so 9.5 true epochs and the labels are off by one (H4.2.3).
- Muon renormalizes each filter to a fixed norm and applies no weight decay, so filter wd is inert. E016's wd effect, if real, came through the head and BN biases.
- Newton-Schulz is already at 3 steps.

Measured mechanisms
- Compile + fused SGD: −14% time (E004).
- Lookahead/EMA: about +1 pp (E005).
- Muon: +0.5 ± 0.3 pp (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: about −20% time, about −0.5 pp (E007).
- Cutting 0.5 epoch: −0.2 pp, −4.8% time (E008).
- Width 576 → 512: −0.25 pp, about −5% time (E010).
- 20 px for 30% of steps plus only 20% at 32 px: −1.2 pp (E011). Both 20 and 24 px give 2×2 group-3 maps, so the cliff comes from total low-resolution exposure and a shorter 32 px tail, not from a map-size threshold.
- Flat (within noise): LS 0.2, Muon lr ×1.5, LR floor 0.
- CUDA graphs and sync removal: about −1% and −0.5%. The systems overhead is exhausted.

Time model
- GPU-bound and close to proportional to pixel-weighted conv MACs, plus a fixed cost of about 0.3 s.
- MACs per 32 px sample: group 1 about 93M (conv3 33M), group 2 about 230M, group 3 about 129M, about 452M in total.
- Levers:
  - group 2 → 320: −15.6% MACs, about −11% time;
  - 28 → 24 px phase: −8% compute, about −6%;
  - drop group-1 conv3: −7% MACs, about −6%;
  - 20 px for the first 15%: −3.5%, about −2.7%;
  - −1 epoch: about −10%.

Accuracy model
- Endpoint averaging dominates. Accuracy is mostly set in the final low-LR 32 px phase, but low-resolution phases are not free (−0.2 to −0.4 pp for 28 → 24 px).
- Exchange rate for every lever: about 0.3-0.5 pp per 10% time. Group-2 width is probably the most expensive per FLOP (the 8×8 feature stage on 100 classes).
- Scalar regularization (head/BN wd) gives at most about 0.1-0.2 pp of true gain.

Strategy
- The true margin is about 0.3-0.4 pp at best. First pin down the true mean with 10 seeds.
- Then spend the margin on the cheapest-per-pp lever, the 24/32 resolution swap, and pair it with time-neutral boosters such as wd or BN recalibration.
- Avoid stacking cuts on top of a single 3-seed reading.

Unsure
- The true mean of the tip.
- Whether kernel reselection in fresh builds shifts accuracy.
- Group-2 width sensitivity.
- Whether BN recalibration after the EMA swap helps.

forecasts.reason: Moving the 28 px steps to 24 px cuts about 8% of pixel compute (about −6% time) for an expected −0.2 to −0.4 pp, which is comparable to the ±0.35 pp reshuffle noise.
E017's identical-math 0.7537 implies E016's true mean is about 0.757, an offset of more than 0.3 pp from 0.7607, outside the H4.1.3 band.
−10% steps gives about −10% time and about −0.4 to −0.7 pp; the noisy base makes the slope unresolvable, and the run is likely infeasible.
−15.6% MACs, but group 2 is the main feature stage for 100 classes; the expected loss of 0.4-0.8 pp exceeds the 0.25 pp limit.
Filter wd is inert (renormalized), so this only further cuts head/BN decay, worth about +0.1 pp at most; it cannot reach E016 + 0.2 pp = 0.7627.
The conv is 33M of 452M MACs (about 7%), so time falls about 6%, below the required 8%, and depth loss costs about 0.3 pp.
A 20 px phase over 15% of steps saves only about 3.5% of pixel compute (about −2.7% time), short of the 4% required.

cruxes: What is the tip recipe's true 10-seed mean: about 0.757 (which leaves about 0.4 pp to spend on time cuts) or about 0.754 (no margin, so the next step must buy accuracy first)?
How much accuracy does 28 px → 24 px cost (I029)? It is the cheapest-looking per-pp time lever, and its result calibrates every resolution and FLOP trade.
Can a time-neutral booster (BN recalibration after the EMA swap, or head/BN weight-decay retuning) reliably buy 0.2-0.3 pp to fund about 10% time cuts?
